outcome: low childbirth self-efficacy for vaginal birth
cohort: The study included 200 high-risk pregnant women with a mean age of 27.74 ± 5.12 years and a mean gestational age of 33.22 ± 4.28 weeks.
finding: Low childbirth self-efficacy for vaginal birth was independently associated with higher maternal age and gestational age.
mod_finding: A history of caesarean section was associated with lower childbirth self-efficacy for vaginal birth.
cross-section timing: During late pregnancy (mean gestational age 33.22 ± 4.28 weeks) between July and December 2022.
gest_age: Mean 33.22 ± 4.28 weeks for the pregnant participants at the time of assessment.
